question: What stool frequency defines diarrhoea clinically?

options.A: Any single episode of nocturnal defaecation
options.B: Passing hard stools every three days
options.C: One bulky stool containing mucus daily
options.D: Three or more loose or liquid stools per day

explanation: The standard clinical definition relies on a change in stool consistency to loose or liquid combined with a frequency threshold of three or more times daily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h1)

question: Which clinical feature primarily distinguishes dysentery from acute watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Complete absence of fever or malaise
options.B: Presence of visible blood in the stool
options.C: Total duration exceeding two full weeks
options.D: Response solely to oral rehydration salts

explanation: Acute bloody diarrhoea or dysentery specifically involves mucosal invasion and ulceration, manifesting visibly as red blood in the stool. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h1)

question: What is the primary mechanism of fluid loss in secretory diarrhoea?

options.A: Complete cessation of renal filtration mechanisms
options.B: Osmotic drawing of water by unabsorbed dietary sugars
options.C: Active secretion of electrolytes into the intestinal lumen
options.D: Physical destruction of the entire muscularis layer

explanation: Secretory toxins stimulate active ion transport out of the mucosal cells into the gut lumen, passively pulling large volumes of water with them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h2)

question: Which acid-base imbalance commonly accompanies severe dehydration from acute watery diarrhoea?
explanation: Massive gastrointestinal loss of bicarbonate-rich fluids directly precipitates a state of metabolic acidosis in the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h2)

question: Which viral pathogen is the most frequent cause of severe dehydrating diarrhoea in infants?
explanation: Rotavirus historically accounts for the majority of severe, acute dehydrating viral gastroenteritis admissions in young children globally. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h3)

question: Why does early cessation of exclusive breastfeeding increase a child's risk of diarrhoeal disease?

options.A: It removes maternal immunological factors and introduces contaminated substitutes
options.B: It stimulates excessive production of gastric hydrochloric acid
options.C: It causes an immediate permanent closure of the pyloric sphincter
options.D: It prevents the normal physiological absorption of dietary lipids

explanation: Breast milk provides passive immunity and clean nutrition; stopping it early exposes the infant to contaminated water and weaning foods before their immune system is mature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h3)

question: A child who is lethargic, has very sunken eyes, and a skin pinch that goes back very slowly is classified under which dehydration category?
explanation: Lethargy, very sunken eyes, and a very slow skin recoil are classic IMCI diagnostic markers for severe dehydration requiring immediate rehydration. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h4)

question: What is the clinical significance of a child drinking eagerly and frantically during a fluid assessment?

options.A: It proves the child is suffering from acute upper respiratory infection
options.B: It demonstrates normal physiological satiety after feeding
options.C: It indicates significant fluid deficit classified as some dehydration
options.D: It signals the complete absence of any systemic electrolyte imbalance

explanation: An eager, thirsty response to being offered fluids reflects moderate body water depletion corresponding to the some dehydration category. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h4)

question: What physiological mechanism allows low-osmolarity ORS to work effectively during secretory diarrhoea?

options.A: Sodium-glucose cotransporters remain functional in the intestinal mucosa
options.B: Direct absorption of dry powder through the gastric wall
options.C: High sugar concentrations completely paralyze intestinal peristalsis
options.D: Neutralization of stomach acid by bicarbonate buffers

explanation: The intestinal sodium-glucose linked transporter uses glucose molecules to pull sodium and water across the brush border epithelium regardless of secretory toxin activity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h5)

question: What is the primary therapeutic rationale for prescribing daily zinc supplementation during acute childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: To provide total caloric requirements when food cannot be tolerated
options.B: To reduce episode duration and prevent recurrence over subsequent months
options.C: To act as a potent broad-spectrum antibiotic against bacterial dysentery
options.D: To instantly stop all vomiting within the first hour of administration

explanation: Zinc accelerates mucosal repair, improves immune response, and decreases both the severity of the current illness and the incidence of future episodes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h5)

question: Why is withholding food during an acute episode of childhood diarrhoea clinically contraindicated?

options.A: It triggers rapid accumulation of fluid in the pleural space
options.B: It permanently damages the endocrine function of the pancreas
options.C: It worsens malnutrition and delays intestinal mucosal repair
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Continued feeding maintains nutritional status and provides necessary building blocks for rapid regeneration of the gastrointestinal epithelium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h6)

question: How should breastfeeding be managed during an episode of acute infant diarrhoea?

options.A: Replaced entirely with undiluted animal milk
options.B: Restricted strictly to once every six hours
options.C: Continued frequently and on demand without interruption
options.D: Halted completely for 48 hours to rest the bowel

explanation: Breast milk is easily digested, provides essential hydration and nutrients, and supplies immunological protection during infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h6)

question: Which clinical finding necessitates immediate transition from oral rehydration to intravenous fluid therapy?

options.A: Mild irritability when the child is disturbed by staff
options.B: Low-grade fever responding rapidly to antipyretics
options.C: A single loose stool passed two hours prior to arrival
options.D: Inability to drink or persistent vomiting of all oral fluids

explanation: When oral intake is impossible due to lethargy, shock, or intractable vomiting, intravenous access is mandatory to restore circulating volume rapidly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h7)

question: When is hospital referral required for a child presenting with acute diarrhoea at a primary clinic?

options.A: When the child shows signs of severe dehydration alongside intractable vomiting
options.B: Only if the parents refuse to administer oral rehydration solutions
options.C: Whenever a child passes more than one loose stool in a single morning
options.D: As soon as zinc supplementation is dispensed for home use

explanation: Severe dehydration coupled with an inability to retain oral fluids requires advanced inpatient supportive care and intravenous resuscitation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h7)

question: Which public health intervention specifically targets the prevention of viral rotavirus gastroenteritis in infants?

options.A: Mandatory quarantine of all school children
options.B: Routine annual administration of anti-malarial drugs

explanation: Rotavirus vaccines are specifically designed and integrated into immunization schedules to prevent severe dehydrating viral gastroenteritis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h8)

question: What is the primary objective of community-level hygiene education regarding handwashing in diarrhoea control?

options.A: To enhance the systemic absorption of oral zinc supplements
options.B: To completely eliminate normal resident skin flora from the hands
options.C: To interrupt the faecal-oral transmission cycle of enteric pathogens
options.D: To stimulate localized sweat gland production in infants

explanation: Washing hands with soap removes pathogens picked up from contaminated environments, effectively breaking the transmission chain to food and water. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h8)
